og_title: Dasha sandhi, the junction between chapters
og_description: The months where one mahadasha hands over to the next. Why astrologers treat them as transitional, all nine transitions, and what to do in one.
h1: dasha sandhi is the doorway between two chapters of ur life
dek: when one mahadasha ends and the next begins, astrologers describe a junction, sandhi, where the old planet is fading and the new one has not settled. it is often felt as restlessness or a change of direction. here is how it works, how long it lasts, and all nine handovers in the cycle.

llms_desc: what dasha sandhi is (the junction between two Vimshottari mahadashas), why it is read as a transitional or unsettled period, the chidra (last antardasha) of each dasha, how long the sandhi is considered to last, the nine mahadasha transitions in the cycle, and practical guidance.

faq.a: the junction between two mahadashas, when one planet's period is ending and the next is beginning. sandhi means junction or joint. astrologers treat it as a transitional time when themes shift.

faq.q: how long does dasha sandhi last?
faq.a: there is no single classical figure. many astrologers treat the last antardasha of the outgoing mahadasha and the first months of the new one as the sandhi, often roughly six months either side of the exact change date.

faq.q: why does dasha sandhi feel unsettled?
faq.a: because the planet that coloured years of ur life is handing over to one with a different nature. a common description is that the old priorities lose their grip before the new ones feel clear.
chidra means gap or hole. some texts call the last antardasha of a mahadasha its chidra and treat it as a sensitive period, since the mahadasha lord is about to step back.

astrologers often single out changes between planets that are natural enemies or very different in nature, such as moon to mars or rahu to jupiter. but the houses each planet rules in ur chart matter more than general rules.
not inherently. it is a transition, and transitions can feel uncomfortable while being exactly what is needed. many people make their biggest changes of direction around a dasha change.

faq.q: does antardasha change also have a sandhi?
faq.a: yes, in smaller form. the junctions between antardashas are shorter and gentler, but some astrologers watch them for timing finer shifts.

faq.q: what should i do during dasha sandhi?
faq.a: traditional advice is to avoid rushing irreversible decisions, to finish what the old period started, and to prepare for the themes of the incoming planet. remedies for both planets are sometimes recommended.

faq.q: how do i know when my mahadasha changes?
faq.a: ur dasha dates come from ur moon's exact position at birth. any vedic chart tool will list them. ask tota shows ur full dasha timeline in the chart desk.

faq.q: is the dasha change date exact?
faq.a: the calculated date is exact for a given birth time and ayanamsa, but a few minutes of birth time error can shift it by days or weeks. treat it as a season, not a single day.
the new mahadasha settles in, usually starting with its own antardasha, the purest expression of the new planet. many people say the new period's character becomes clear a few months in.

faq.q: is dasha sandhi mentioned in classical texts?
faq.a: the idea of junctions, sandhi, is used across jyotish, for example in gandanta between signs. the specific treatment of dasha junctions is developed more in later and modern practice than in a single classical rule.
